paragraphs.text: Run opencode as an ACP subagent in DeepSeek Harness — delegation tool, settings page, run history.
# dsh-opencode-acp
Run opencode as an ACP subagent inside DeepSeek Harness (DSH).
Your main agent keeps its own model and context; `subagent_opencode` hands a self-contained task to
opencode in a separate process, opencode does the work with **its own models, tools and free tier**,
and only the final answer comes back. A settings page lets you switch models, choose the permission
policy and working directory, and watch every run — including the opencode session id, duration and

orking directory, and watch every run — including the opencode session id, duration and
token usage.
中文说明 · **官网** · self-hosted copy (both Chinese by default, `EN` switch top right)
## Quick start

1. Install: `dsh plugin --profile default add dsh-opencode-acp`, then restart or refresh DSH.
2. Ope

n **Settings → OpenCode 委派**; keep the default model and press **刷新列表** to pull
opencode's current c

atalog, then **测试模型** to confirm one actually answers.
3. Ask your agent: *"Delegate to subagent_ope

ncode: create hello.txt and tell me what you wrote."*
The call returns a child id immediately; the c

ompletion notice carries opencode's answer and the
run appears in the history with its opencode sess
ion id, duration and tokens.
## Why
- **Two harnesses, one conversation.** DSH stays the driver. opencode brings its own free models and

its own tooling; nothing it does lands in your context or your token bill.
- **You can see what hap

pened.** Because this plugin speaks ACP itself, each run records the remote
session id, the model, t

he duration, tool-call count and token usage — so "which opencode session
was that?" has an answer.

- **Settings without restarts.** Settings are read at the start of every delegation, so a saved
chan
ge applies to the next run.
## Requirements
| DeepSeek Harness | `>=0.2.1-rc.1 <0.3.0` (declared as `engines.dsh`; install refuses other version

s) |
| opencode | v2 with the `acp` subcommand (`opencode --version`, `opencode acp --help`) |
| ope
ncode auth | already logged in (`opencode auth login`); the child reuses your login and free models
code auth | already logged in (`opencode auth login`); the child reuses your login and free models |

The child gets only your task text and the working directory — never your conversation.
## Settings
| Group | Setting | Meaning |

| Model | main model | Picker built from the models your opencode has used, plus a free-form id |
|

Model | small model | opencode's model for titles and small jobs (blank = let opencode choose) |
| M

odel | health check | Runs `opencode --version` and reports whether the executable resolves |
| Mode
l | test model | Starts one throwaway session against the **saved** model and answers whether it wor

ks right now (it spends one real request) |
| Model | refresh list | Runs `opencode models` and merg
es the free-tier entries into the picker; cached in `catalog.json`, so it costs one short subprocess

, not a request. The page also refreshes by itself once when the cache is more than 6 hours old. |
|

Execution | permission | `allow` auto-answers permission requests, `reject` denies them |
| Executi

on | working directory | Follow the calling session, or pin one path |
| Advanced | command / args |

The opencode executable plus the `acp` argument |
| Advanced | grace | Process teardown window in m

illiseconds |
| Advanced | env | Extra environment variables as a JSON object |
Settings live in `$DSH_HOME/opencode-acp/settings.json`; runs in `runs.json` beside it (last 100).
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- The ACP protocol carries no model parameter, so the model is decided on the opencode side. This
pl

ugin injects `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` into the child; `OPENCODE_CONFIG` (a file path) is
ignored by

`opencode acp` in v2 — verified, not assumed.
- Runs are one-shot: an external ACP child cannot rec

eive follow-up messages, so it is not
continuable. For multi-turn delegation use DSH's built-in `sub

agent` instead.
- The child process runs with your user account and is **not** confined by the DSH s

andbox, exactly
like DSH's own `@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent-acp`. Treat delegation as "opencode may do

what you
could do".
## Troubleshooting
| Symptom | Cause and fix |
| Delegation fails with `category: free-limit` | opencode's free tier is exhausted for the account.

Click **测试模型** to see which model works now, or connect a provider in opencode. |
| Delegation fails
with `category: provider.internal` + `Authentication required` | that model's provider is not logge

d in on the opencode side: run `opencode auth login`, or pick another model |
| Delegation fails wit
h `category: provider.internal` + `Model is unavailable` | that model's endpoint is down right now;

pick another one |
| The settings page shows a read error or is blank | the Host could not register
`/.dsh-opencode-acp/*`. Restart DSH; if it persists, check that the bundle is enabled in Plugins. |
| `卡住` on a delegation that never returns | fixed in 0.3.0: a child that dies mid-request now fails

the run instead of leaving it pending |
| Windows: `EPERM ... rename ... state.json` from another pl
ugin | two DSH instances writing the same profile state. Quit from the tray and start once. |
The `/.dsh-opencode-acp/*` routes are **unauthenticated by design** and reachable from any process o

n
this machine (localhost only). Run history and settings are stored as plain JSON under
`$DSH_HOME/
opencode-acp/`; treat that directory as sensitive as your shell history.
## Limits

- Only assistant text is returned; opencode's tool traffic, reasoning and plans stay in its own
sess

ion.
- A fresh process per run: expect a few seconds of startup on every delegation.
- Windows, macO

S and Linux are all supported. The default command is the npm-global opencode on
